name: LangGraph
description: A library for building stateful, multi-actor applications with LLMs, built on top of LangChain. Provides native support for cyclic graphs, conditional routing, persistent state, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
key_capabilities: Stateful graph-based agent orchestration
Cyclic and conditional workflow support
Built-in persistence and checkpointing
Human-in-the-loop interaction patterns
Parallel node execution
Streaming support for real-time output
Native integration with LangChain tools and models
pros: Purpose-built for complex multi-agent workflows with cycles and conditional logic
First-class state management with TypedDict state schemas
Excellent debugging and visualization tools (LangSmith integration)
Active development with frequent updates and strong community
Supports both sync and async execution patterns
cons: Relatively new library with evolving API surface
Tight coupling to LangChain ecosystem may limit flexibility
Learning curve for graph-based programming paradigm
Limited production deployment tooling compared to cloud-native solutions
compliance_notes: LangGraph itself does not handle compliance directly but supports building compliant workflows through state-based audit trails, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and integration with observability platforms like LangSmith for tracing and monitoring.

name: LangChain
description: A framework for developing applications powered by language models. Provides abstractions for chains, agents, memory, and tool use, with integrations across major LLM providers and vector stores.
key_capabilities: Chain composition for sequential LLM workflows
Agent framework with tool-use capabilities
Memory management (conversation, summary, buffer)
Document loading and text splitting utilities
Vector store integrations for RAG patterns
Output parsing and structured generation
Multi-provider model abstraction layer
pros: Largest ecosystem of integrations (150+ LLM providers, vector stores, tools)
Well-documented with extensive examples and tutorials
Flexible abstraction layer supports rapid prototyping
Strong community and active development
LangSmith provides production observability and evaluation
cons: Abstraction overhead can make debugging difficult
Chain-based paradigm less suited for complex cyclic workflows
Performance overhead from abstraction layers in latency-sensitive applications
Some integrations are community-maintained with varying quality
compliance_notes: LangChain supports compliance through callback handlers for logging, LangSmith for tracing and audit trails, and configurable retry/fallback mechanisms. Does not provide built-in data residency controls; these must be configured at the model provider level.

name: Semantic Kernel
description: An open-source SDK from Microsoft for integrating LLMs into applications. Supports C#, Python, and Java with native Azure OpenAI integration and enterprise-grade plugin architecture.
key_capabilities: Plugin-based architecture for modular AI capabilities
Native Azure OpenAI and OpenAI integration
Planner for automatic function orchestration
Memory and embedding management
Prompt template engine with semantic functions
Multi-language support (C#, Python, Java)
Enterprise patterns for dependency injection and configuration
pros: Deep integration with Microsoft and Azure ecosystem
Enterprise-ready with familiar .NET patterns and dependency injection
Strong typing and plugin architecture promotes maintainable code
Active Microsoft backing ensures long-term support
Good fit for organizations already invested in Microsoft stack
cons: Python SDK less mature than C# counterpart
Smaller community compared to LangChain ecosystem
Planner capabilities still evolving and can be unpredictable
Fewer third-party integrations outside Microsoft ecosystem
compliance_notes: Semantic Kernel inherits compliance capabilities from Azure OpenAI Service when used together, including data privacy, content filtering, and abuse monitoring. Supports enterprise authentication via Microsoft Entra ID and integrates with Azure governance tools.

name: Amazon Bedrock Agents
description: A fully managed service for building AI agents that can reason, plan, and execute multi-step tasks using foundation models. Integrates natively with AWS services for action execution and knowledge base retrieval.
key_capabilities: Managed agent runtime with automatic reasoning and planning
Action groups for integrating with AWS Lambda and APIs
Knowledge base integration with RAG capabilities
Guardrails for content filtering and topic control
Session management for multi-turn conversations
Native integration with AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, Lambda)
Model selection across multiple foundation model providers
pros: Fully managed service eliminates infrastructure management overhead
Native AWS integration simplifies enterprise deployment
Built-in guardrails provide content safety and compliance controls
Supports multiple foundation models (Claude, Llama, Titan, etc.)
Pay-per-use pricing with no upfront commitments
Data never leaves AWS account boundary
cons: Limited to AWS ecosystem and regions where Bedrock is available
Less flexibility for custom orchestration patterns compared to code-first frameworks
Agent behavior can be opaque and difficult to debug
Newer service with fewer production case studies
Action group configuration can be complex for non-trivial workflows
compliance_notes: Bedrock Agents inherits AWS compliance certifications. Data processed by Bedrock is not used to train models and does not leave the customer's AWS account. Supports VPC endpoints for private connectivity, AWS PrivateLink, and encryption at rest and in transit. Guardrails provide configurable content filtering aligned with responsible AI principles.
